03 / Enumeration, equilibrium & keeping the experiment honest

One radius at a time

The observation square spans −6 to +6 m. Centres start one displayed radius inside the edge. Grid spacing equals that radius. Rows run from top to bottom, columns from left to right. The first trial is red at cell 0, green at cell 1, blue at cell 2. Blue advances first; after exhausting its remaining cells, green advances and blue starts immediately after green. Red advances last.

For n cells on each axis there are N = n² positions and N(N−1)(N−2)/6 distinct triples. The ordering uses red index < green index < blue index, omitting the six equivalent colour assignments for equal masses. Reflections, rotations and translations remain in the scan, so distinct arrangements may look similar. A finite grid eventually ends; it does not provide infinitely new motion.

The masses are mathematical points. Displayed radius sets spacing and appearance, not a solid collision surface; adjacent circles can overlap visually. Close encounters are handled by a separate 0.015 m centre-separation threshold.

Rest starts and orbit candidates

All three start at zero velocity. Each integration step combines the other two pulls for every body, then updates all three velocities and positions. Acceleration is aᵢ = μ Σⱼ≠ᵢ (rⱼ − rᵢ) / |rⱼ − rᵢ|³ with μ = 9.80665 m³/s², giving 1g from one body at 1 m. No Earth field, fixed body, wall force, initial push, friction or softening is added.

“Bounded” means no body left the square during the test. It does not mean an equilibrium orbit. “Orbit candidate” requires at least three repeating cycles of the full centre-of-mass-relative position and velocity state, sampled phase agreement within 2% of characteristic position/velocity scales, appreciable motion, and energy drift ≤0.1%. Detection is conservative and can miss orbits; it is not a stability proof.

Starting at rest gives zero total angular momentum, conserved under mutual gravity. A non-degenerate rigidly rotating equilibrium has angular momentum Iω ≠ 0, so this rest-start experiment cannot reach that particular kind of orbit. No circular-orbit claim is made. Symmetric forces can also leave one body stationary. Equations and conserved quantities ↗

All escapes, plus interactions lasting more than five seconds

Every arrangement is computed and recorded, but automatic playback includes every escaped outcome, regardless of duration, plus other trials whose recorded physical simulation time is strictly greater than 5 seconds. A non-escaped trial ending at or before 5 seconds is skipped visually and the scan immediately continues. This threshold measures simulated interaction time, not slowed animation or wall-clock time. The simulation time limit must exceed 5 seconds. A trial can stop because of escape, close encounter, numerical failure, or the time limit; its stopping reason stays visible.

The fullscreen display is a browser screensaver-style view. Exit with the button or Escape. The page must remain open and the device awake: browser background throttling or operating-system sleep can pause it. The scan position is checkpointed after recording each short trial or fully displaying each qualifying trial. On reload the last unfinished qualifying animation may repeat. Qualifying animations use the minimum display duration and replay speed, with brief start and final dwells. The log includes all escapes and hides other short trials by default; its explicit checkbox makes all recorded evidence available for manual review.

Evidence and numerical limits

Adaptive kick–drift–kick velocity Verlet integration uses smaller timesteps near close approaches. Variable steps weaken its usual symplectic guarantees. Relative energy drift is normalized by max(|E₀|, μ) in unit-mass energy units. Close encounters, >1% energy drift, extremely small timesteps and the 2-million-step limit stop a trial separately from escape. Finite test duration and collision stopping limit what can be inferred about later motion.

Starting states, settings, trajectories, outcome and final image are stored in this browser for every completed trial, including orbit candidates. Records are read a page at a time. On a storage failure the scan stops instead of silently deleting evidence. Export CSV for all logged summaries, the latest 1,000 replays for a bounded archive, or all orbit-candidate replays with the separate button. Export archives before clearing the log. Saved scan position is separate from the log.

Earlier/imported results keep their original starting velocities and labels. Older bounded records are not upgraded into orbit candidates. Back up browser-local evidence regularly.
